subject.title: [Bug]: `openclaw models auth login` on node host writes OAuth token locally instead of syncing to gateway

question: Should this bug be fixed by fail-closing `models auth login` on remote node hosts, or by designing gateway-side credential forwarding?
rationale: Both options prevent wrong-host credential writes, but forwarding OAuth/provider credentials across the node-gateway boundary is a larger security and protocol decision, while the existing maintainer draft favored fail-closed gateway-host login.

options.title: Fail-closed gateway-host login
options.body: Block provider auth login on node hosts pointed at non-loopback gateways and instruct users to run auth on the gateway host; this matches the prior maintainer draft and is the narrowest safe fix.

options.title: Design credential forwarding
options.body: Keep node-host login as a supported workflow only after adding an explicit, reviewed gateway credential-forwarding API and threat model.

options.title: Defer until linked PR is resolved
options.body: Leave the issue open but do not queue replacement work until maintainers decide whether to adopt, replace, or close the conflicting fork PR.

recommendation.title: Fail-closed gateway-host login
recommendation.body: Block provider auth login on node hosts pointed at non-loopback gateways and instruct users to run auth on the gateway host; this matches the prior maintainer draft and is the narrowest safe fix.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent already pushed and verified the prior maintainer follow-up for this exact fail-closed direction.
